limitations_and_boundaries: The experiments were done in the context of model selection, so the only real difference between the two spaces is connectivity.

The goal of the search algorithm is to identify the model with the highest possible score; comparing search algorithms based on a predictive score is somewhat misleading because differences in this score are dependent on the quality of the scoring criterion.
The degree to which multiple representations will be a problem is highly dependent on the states visited by the search algorithm.
The results are based on a greedy search algorithm; more sophisticated search algorithms are likely to benefit more from searching in E-space.

missed_core_items.description: The scoring criterion used is the BDeu criterion with a prior equivalent sample size of ten and a structure prior of 0.001^f, where f is the number of free parameters.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: We used a Bayesian scoring criterion for discrete variables in all of our experiments. The criterion, called the BDeu criterion, is derived by Heckerman et al. (1995).5 The criterion measures the relative posterior probability that the distribution from which the data was generated has the independence constraints given in the DAG. The BDeu criterion uses a parameter prior that has uniform means, and requires both a prior equivalence sample size and a structure prior. For all of our experiments, we used a prior equivalent sample size of ten, and a structure prior of 0.001f, where f is the number of free parameters in the DAG.

missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Greedy search is a simple algorithm that, given the current state, always moves to the adjacent state that increases the score the most. If no adjacent state has a higher score, the algorithm terminates.

experiments_or_tasks: Apply greedy search algorithm in B-space (individual DAGs) and E-space (equivalence classes) starting from the empty graph, using a score-equivalent criterion, on six datasets: MSWeb, Nielsen, EachMovie, Media Metrix, HouseVotes, Mushroom. Record score per training case, holdout score, and elapsed time at each step.

methods.name: Greedy search in B-space
methods.protocol_description: Greedy search algorithm applied to the space of individual Bayesian-network structures (DAGs) using a score-equivalent criterion, starting from the empty graph. At each step, the algorithm considers local operators (edge addition, deletion, reversal) and moves to the highest-scoring neighbor.

methods.name: Greedy search in E-space
methods.protocol_description: Greedy search algorithm applied to the space of equivalence classes of Bayesian-network structures, represented as PDAGs, using a score-equivalent criterion, starting from the empty graph. Operators are defined on equivalence classes (e.g., edge addition, deletion) and scored locally.
